set.body:
Implement coordinate-bearing non-spatial axes and neutral serializable records.

Design requirements
- AxisCoordinates supports Ordinal, Regular(origin, step, unit), Explicit(values, unit), and Categorical(labels).
- Extent is derived from coordinates; explicit and categorical payloads are immutable and have content-based equality/hash behavior.
- AxisKind is extensible through a validated custom identifier.
- AxisUnit has standard identifiers plus custom identifiers without becoming a general units-of-measure framework.
- Axis identity, persistent identity, and coordinate equivalence are distinct concepts.
- Slice timing, BIDS entities, gradient tables, phase-encoding policy, and acquisition protocols remain outside core.
- Define AxisRecord suitable for persistence and compatibility checks.

Acceptance criteria
- Time axes distinguish 800 ms, 2 s, and irregular schedules.
- Echo, frequency, trial, channel, and coil axes can retain their sampled coordinates or categorical labels.
- Coordinate lookup is total for a checked index and selection reports the selected coordinate.
- Duplicate-name and malformed-coordinate failures remain typed.
- JVM and Scala.js APIs are behaviorally identical.

Tests
- ScalaCheck laws: coordinate count equals extent; Regular lookup equals origin + index * step; Explicit and Categorical lookup return the declared element.
- Content equality/hash regression for independently allocated equal explicit arrays and categorical arrays.
- Round-trip properties for every AxisRecord variant, standard/custom kinds, and standard/custom units.
- Negative cases: zero extent, empty explicit/categorical payload, non-finite origin/step/value, zero step where forbidden, invalid custom ids, duplicate axis names.
- Axis selection removes exactly one axis and preserves all remaining coordinate records and order.
- Random axis permutations preserve coordinate/value correspondence.
- JVM/Scala.js differential fixtures use identical serialized records and checksums.
set.title: Give non-spatial axes coordinate sampling and stable records
